lineage: A FIFO with full/empty flags and (in the async case) gray-coded pointers is the standard backpressure/flow-control element between two clock or rate domains -- it holds state and asserts 'full' to stall a fast producer
version: github.com/freecores/generic_fifos master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)
build_system: iverilog + a Techne testbench exercising fill/drain and the full/empty flags
entry_points: the FIFO module: push/pop with full/empty/level outputs

example.command: Techne testbench: push until 'full' asserts (backpressure), pop until 'empty', check no overflow/underflow and correct FIFO order
example.output: the full/empty flag timeline; in-order data out

upstream_docs: Cummings, Simulation and Synthesis Techniques for Asynchronous FIFO Design

human_capability_summary.built_to: buffer data between a producer and consumer running at different rates, asserting 'full' to stall the producer and 'empty' to stall the consumer -- flow control in hardware
human_capability_summary.pressure: a producer and consumer with mismatched, bursty rates; without backpressure a fast producer overruns and data is lost
human_capability_summary.success_means: no overflow or underflow, in-order delivery, correct flags across the rate mismatch

known_human_problem_solved: rate-decoupling and backpressure between hardware blocks
human_environmental_pressure: rate mismatch and burstiness between producer and consumer; bounded buffer depth
human_failure_condition: overflow (fast producer, ignored 'full') drops data; underflow (consumer reads 'empty') reads garbage -- silent corruption downstream
behavioral_entry_point: push faster than you pop until 'full' asserts, then confirm the producer is stalled and no data is lost; the flags are the observable decisions
